paper.abstract_en: We investigate the performance of a gate teleportation protocol in the presence of realistic noise by considering bit-flip, phase-flip, depolarizing, and amplitude-damping channels acting on each qubit after every gate operation. The teleportation fidelity is evaluated as a function of the noise parameter for different input-state configurations. Our results demonstrate a systematic degradation of fidelity with increasing noise strength, with the magnitude of the degradation depending on both the noise model and the input state. The bit-flip and phase-flip channels exhibit pronounced state-dependent behavior, whereas depolarizing noise leads to comparatively similar fidelity degradation for the considered states. Amplitude damping produces a distinct decrease in fidelity associated with energy dissipation during the teleportation process. These results provide a comparative assessment of the noise sensitivity, robustness, and relative state-dependent degradation of gate teleportation relevant to noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices.
